title: Musée des Beaux-Arts de Rouen: Masterpieces
subtitle: Twenty works at the Musée des Beaux-Arts, from changing weather to portraits and invented encounters with the past.
introduction:
Monet's cathedral fills the picture almost to its edges. Pissarro's bridge remains a route through a city of smoke, traffic and evening light. Both represent Rouen, but they assign it different scales of attention: one holds a façade close, the other gives urban movement a broader field.

The Musée des Beaux-Arts selection extends well beyond images of the city. Portraits ask how clothing and posture identify people; large historical and mythological scenes distribute authority or violence through a setting. Delaroche's imprisoned Joan of Arc is especially useful for distinguishing a compelling image from a reliable record of an event. These twenty works reward that distinction between what is convincingly painted and what is historically established.
visitNote: Check the museum's current opening information and displays before travelling. The guide draws on the collection; loans, conservation and changes of hanging can affect what is available to see.

books.title: Impressionism: A Centenary Exhibition
books.author: Anne Dayez, Michel Hoog and Charles S. Moffett
books.note: The Metropolitan Museum's Impressionism: A Centenary Exhibition provides entries and historical essays for the painters represented here by Monet, Pissarro and Sisley. Read it alongside the contrasting views of Rouen and the Seine.

works.title: Hill Path in Sunlight
works.credit: Alfred Sisley. Hill Path in Sunlight. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/alfred-sisley/hill-path-in-sunlight-1891
works.description: The rising path gives the small walkers a route and the landscape a direction. Warm grass and scattered trees establish the slope beneath a much larger blue sky. The people are consequential as a measure of the ascent, though their scale keeps the ordinary walk from becoming the only subject of the view.

works.title: Male Academy Study, Seated and Seen from Behind
works.catalogueTitle: Male 'académie' Seated and Seen from Behind
works.credit: Male 'académie' Seated and Seen from Behind. WikiArt; Théodore Géricault. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: The model's back carries most of the information about the pose. Light clarifies its relation to the raised arm while the compressed legs support the seated body below. Without relying on the face, the study makes a bodily position intelligible through pressure, balance and the connections between parts.

works.title: Portrait of Jacques-Émile Blanche
works.credit: John Singer Sargent. Portrait of Jacques-Emile Blanche. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/john-singer-sargent/portrait-of-jacques-emile-blanche
works.description: The hand crossing the chest introduces a less rigid element within the grey coat's broad shape. A pale shirt and green background separate the sitter into distinct areas without overfilling the setting. Sargent gives the face sharper attention while allowing the surrounding clothing to remain more broadly handled.

works.title: Madame Aymon, Known as La Belle Zélie
works.catalogueTitle: Portrait of Madame Aymon, La belle Zélie
works.credit: Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres. Portrait of Madame Aymon, La belle Zélie. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/jean-auguste-dominique-ingres/portrait-of-madame-aymon-la-belle-z%C3%A9lie-1806
works.description: The oval boundary answers the curls, shawl and the turn of the face with another enclosing curve. Firm edges keep those shapes distinct, giving the likeness an emphatic design. Instead of separating dress from identity, the portrait makes their arrangement part of what allows this particular sitter to register.

works.title: Venus and Cupid
works.credit: Lavinia Fontana. Venus and Cupid. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Cupid's approach to Venus's cheek brings the mythological pair into unusually close quarters. Pearls, veil and embroidered fabric receive enough distinction to recall the attention of a portrait. The scene's intimacy comes from proximity and detailed surfaces; it does not require the traditional identification of a particular model to be treated as certain.

works.title: Portrait of a Carabinier
works.credit: Portrait of a Carabinier. WikiArt; Théodore Géricault. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: The polished breastplate gives the torso a hard surface that contrasts with the living face and hand. The large hat occupies further space beside the soldier, so military equipment remains conspicuous without completely enclosing him. Géricault holds the individual and the professional role together through these different kinds of surface.

works.title: Burial of a Sailor in a Village in La Manche
works.catalogueTitle: Burial of a Sailor in a Manche Village
works.credit: August Hagborg. Burial of a Sailor in a Manche Village. Image credit: August Hagborg; Source credit: Musée des Beaux-Arts de Rouen. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The road allows a funeral to extend beyond one tightly grouped cluster of mourners. Separate villagers belong to the procession at different distances, while the ordinary settlement remains around them. Hagborg locates collective loss within a place people continue to inhabit, rather than isolating mourning from the daily landscape.

works.title: Diomedes Devoured by His Horses
works.credit: Gustave Moreau. DIOMEDE DEVORE PAR SES CHEVAUX. WikiArt: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop.
works.description: The enormous ruin threatens to outweigh the small figures and horses beneath it. A violent subject is therefore not offered as one immediately legible encounter. Attention must move through architectural scale and dark openings to locate the action, making the setting an active obstacle to a quick reading of the myth.

works.title: Joan of Arc Ill and Questioned in Prison
works.catalogueTitle: Jeanne d’Arc malade est interrogée dans sa prison par le cardinal de Winchester
works.credit: Paul Delaroche; WikiArt
works.description: The cardinal's red robes occupy the cell with a weight that contrasts with Joan's more restricted position. The scene is historical invention: the museum notes that Winchester never visited her in prison. Delaroche uses the imagined encounter to make unequal power visible, not to provide an eyewitness account of an interrogation.

works.title: Rouen Cathedral: The Portal and Albane Tower, Grey Weather
works.catalogueTitle: La Cathédrale de Rouen. Le Portail et la tour d’Albane. Temps gris
works.credit: Claude Monet; WikiArt
works.description: The close crop excludes nearly all the surrounding city, allowing the façade to occupy the painted field. Grey and blue-violet marks turn stone into a record of atmospheric change. The museum dates this canvas 1894, while explaining that the cathedral series was worked on in 1892–1893 and dated later—a useful distinction between a painted view and its inscribed year.

works.title: The Justice of Trajan
works.credit: Eugène Delacroix. La Justice de Trajan. Image credit: Eugène Delacroix; Source credit: Musée des Beaux-Arts de Rouen. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Proportional resize and JPEG compression; full source frame retained.
works.description: The bright horse helps locate Trajan within the crossing gestures, banners and crowd. Authority is presented through a moving, public encounter rather than a ruler alone on a throne. The surrounding figures remain necessary to the image: a judgment has to be enacted before people, not merely declared through the emperor's likeness.

works.title: The Virgin and Blessing Child
works.credit: Шарль Андре Ван Лоо. La Vierge et l'enfant bénissant. Image credit: Charles André van Loo. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The child's raised hand is separated clearly enough from the background to read as a blessing. Mary supports his standing body, joining that ceremonial gesture to a practical relation of care. The small group's closeness makes spiritual authority appear through a dependent child rather than through an isolated, commanding figure.

works.title: Lady's Cove, Wales
works.credit: Alfred Sisley. Lady’s Cove, Pays de Galles. Image credit: Alfred Sisley; Source credit: https://www.alfredsisley.org/the-complete-works.html?ps=96&pageno=9. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Proportional resize and JPEG compression; full source frame retained.
works.description: Successive bands of surf describe different distances from the rocks and headland. The coastline remains comparatively firm while the water breaks into changing marks. Sisley uses that contrast to keep movement measurable: waves can alter from moment to moment without making the shore's recession impossible to follow.

works.title: The Marriage of Cupid and Psyche
works.catalogueTitle: Le Mariage de l'Amour et Psyché
works.credit: François Boucher. Le Mariage de l'Amour et Psyché. Image credit: François Boucher. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The figures form an open curve across the clouds, with gaps that prevent the celestial company from becoming a solid crowd. Smaller winged bodies and drapery extend the assembly without giving it an earthly platform. Suspension is part of the design; the spaces between the bodies help the celebration appear unweighted.

works.title: Pont Boieldieu, Rouen: Sunset, Misty Weather
works.catalogueTitle: Le Pont Boieldieu à Rouen, soleil couchant, temps brumeux
works.credit: Camille Pissarro. Le Pont Boieldieu à Rouen, soleil couchant, temps brumeux. Image credit: Camille Pissarro; Source credit: http://mbarouen.fr/fr/oeuvres/le-pont-boieldieu-a-rouen-soleil-couchant-temps-brumeux. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Proportional resize and JPEG compression; full source frame retained.
works.description: The bridge provides a clear diagonal through smoke and evening haze. People and vehicles remain small marks along that route, connecting the atmospheric view to ordinary traffic. Pissarro makes a working city legible without separating industry from weather: both contribute to the air through which the river and buildings are seen.

works.title: The Church at Moret in Full Sunlight
works.credit: Alfred Sisley. L’Eglise de Moret (plein soleil). Image credit: Alfred Sisley; Source credit: The Yorck Project (2002) 10.000 Meisterwerke der Malerei (DVD-ROM), distributed by DIRECTMEDIA Publishing GmbH. ISBN : 3936122202 .. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Proportional resize and JPEG compression; full source frame retained.
works.description: Yellow stone and blue-violet shadow divide the same church into areas of different temperature. Small awnings and figures locate it within a street, while the crop gives its walls considerable scale. The building provides a fixed arrangement on which the changing conditions of sunlight can become conspicuous.

works.title: A Game of Cards
works.credit: Judith Leyster. A Game of Cards. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The woman in red turns toward the space outside the players' circle, while another participant makes cards visible. Their gathering is already underway, yet these gestures open it to an additional observer. Leyster gives sociability several directions at once; no single gaze explains all the relations around the barrel-table.

works.title: Solemn Mass in Honour of Henry III
works.catalogueTitle: Messe solennelle en l'honneur d'Henri III
works.credit: Herman van der Mast. Messe solennelle en l'honneur d'Henri III. Image credit: David.Monniaux; Own work. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Messe_solennelle_en_pr%C3%A9sence_dHenri_III_IMG_7446.jpg. CC0 (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/). Full-frame resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: Kneeling and standing groups take different positions within the church, using posture and clothing to distinguish their roles. Architecture leads toward the ceremony farther inside and gives the assembly a common order. The scene can accommodate many participants without requiring each to become an individually isolated portrait.

works.title: Portrait of Paul Valéry
works.credit: Jacques-Émile Blanche. Portrait de Paul Valéry. Image credit: Jacques-Émile Blanche. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The hand against Valéry's cheek gives the head a physical support and breaks the upright formality of the seated pose. A patterned red ground surrounds the pale face. The gesture may suggest thought, but cannot reveal its content; the portrait's strength lies in a particular arrangement rather than an invented account of the writer's mind.

works.title: Saint Genevieve before Paris
works.credit: Charles Le Brun. Sainte Geneviève devant Paris. Image credit: Charles Le Brun. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The saint's reading takes place beneath an angel while Paris remains visible at a distance. That relation connects an apparently secluded devotional act to a city beyond it. Light concentrates on the figures, but the urban setting keeps their significance from remaining wholly private or confined to the immediate foreground.

closingSections.title: Take one comparison into the city
paragraphs: After studying Monet's cathedral or Pissarro's bridge, a present-day view can clarify how much each painting selects. It will not reproduce the artist's position, weather or historical surroundings exactly. Confirm current museum displays separately, especially if one work is the main reason for a visit.
